title: Liquidity percentile by session
instructions: For every trading day, append a new column liq_pct with the percentile rank of volume within that same day.
hint: Work inside out. Rank tickers only against other tickers on the same day, and express rank on the 0–1 percentile scale.

explanation.meaning: Rank tickers only against other tickers on the same day, and express rank on the 0–1 percentile scale.
Attach one percentile to each original row, preserving the long panel.

title: Cross-sectional residual returns
instructions: Return a Series of each asset return minus the mean return of assets traded on the same date.
hint: Work inside out. Broadcast the per-date average back to every row on that date; transform preserves the original row count.

explanation.meaning: Broadcast the per-date average back to every row on that date; transform preserves the original row count.
Subtract the contemporaneous cross-sectional mean from each observation.

title: Sector-neutral residual returns
instructions: Return returns after removing each date-and-sector mean return, preserving the original row order.
hint: Work inside out. Form groups specific to each session AND sector; the same sector on another date is a different group.

explanation.meaning: Form groups specific to each session AND sector; the same sector on another date is a different group.
Align each group mean back with the original rows.
Create residual returns with no inadvertent reordering.

title: Cross-sectional trade candidates
instructions: For each date, retain only the two highest-volume tickers; return date, ticker and volume sorted by date and descending volume.
hint: Work inside out. Put each day in order and move the most liquid stocks first within its day.

explanation.meaning: Put each day in order and move the most liquid stocks first within its day.
Select two rows FROM EACH DATE, not just two rows in total.
Project only the requested columns.

title: Normalize factor exposures
instructions: Return a Series of beta divided by its date-level mean beta (one normalized exposure per row).
hint: Work inside out. Replicate the average beta for each date alongside every asset exposure.

explanation.meaning: Replicate the average beta for each date alongside every asset exposure.
Normalize each asset by its own date benchmark, without a loop.

title: Dollar-volume feature matrix
instructions: Compute close × volume for each record, pivot into dates × tickers, and sort the columns alphabetically.
hint: Work inside out. Multiply price and quantity row-by-row to build a turnover proxy.

explanation.meaning: Multiply price and quantity row-by-row to build a turnover proxy.
Make a date-by-ticker feature matrix from the long panel.
Sort ticker columns, leaving date rows intact.

title: Standardized latent-state signal
instructions: Return a Series of the signal standardized using its entire sample mean and population standard deviation.
hint: Work inside out. Compute the scalar signal center.

explanation.meaning: Compute the scalar signal center.
Use population standard deviation (not pandas default ddof=1).
Subtract center and divide scale at every date. This full-sample version is descriptive, NOT safe for live trading.

title: Causal z-score feature
instructions: Return signal minus its previous 5-day mean, divided by its previous 5-day std; use at least 3 earlier observations.
hint: Work inside out. Make historical window end at yesterday, avoiding current-day information leakage.

explanation.meaning: Make historical window end at yesterday, avoiding current-day information leakage.
Form trailing windows, requiring three past observations.
Measure current signal relative to a strictly historical distribution.

title: Regime-weighted forecast
instructions: Return a Series of probability-weighted forecasts, treating the stress-regime forecast as -0.5 × forecast.
hint: Work inside out. Probabilities form the time-dependent mixture weights.

explanation.meaning: Probabilities form the time-dependent mixture weights.
Combine one optimistic forecast and a scaled defensive forecast elementwise across dates.

title: Bounded trading signal
instructions: Cap the signal at ±{cap}, then lag it by one session to construct next-day usable exposure.
hint: Work inside out. Limit extreme exposure before execution.

explanation.meaning: Limit extreme exposure before execution.
At row t, show the signal that was known at t−1, not the signal computed at t.

title: Encode sector membership
instructions: Return a one-hot Boolean DataFrame of sectors with columns sorted alphabetically.
hint: Work inside out. Convert one categorical sector per stock into indicator columns.

explanation.meaning: Convert one categorical sector per stock into indicator columns.
Make the feature column order deterministic for downstream models.

title: Cross-sectional return rank matrix
instructions: Rank returns by date, with rank 1 for the highest return, then pivot into dates × tickers.
hint: Work inside out. Rank within each date; larger returns receive smaller ranks.

explanation.meaning: Rank within each date; larger returns receive smaller ranks.
Attach ranks to the long panel without losing other columns.
Turn the normalized feature into a time-by-asset matrix.

title: Rank normalized daily signals
instructions: Within each date, calculate demeaned returns and then rank them descending within date as a Series, with rank 1 best.
hint: Work inside out. Demean returns independently for each trading day, preserving original row alignment.

explanation.meaning: Demean returns independently for each trading day, preserving original row alignment.
Rank the cross-sectional residuals within their own date, not globally.

title: Sector-neutral liquidity filter
instructions: Return ticker, date, ret, volume for Tech-sector records with volume above their SAME-DATE sector average.
hint: Work inside out. Compute a sector-relative daily volume benchmark aligned with every observation.

explanation.meaning: Compute a sector-relative daily volume benchmark aligned with every observation.
Require Tech classification and unusually high volume together.
